subject.title: refactor(auth): finish SQLite-only auth profile cutover

question: Should OpenClaw approve the compatibility contract in which `AuthStorage.create(path)` and `FileAuthStorageBackend` remain callable but stop using their named file as the persistence location during the deprecation window?
rationale: This is a deliberate public Plugin SDK behavior change, not a mechanical correctness defect: preserving old file semantics conflicts with the repository’s SQLite-only runtime policy, while changing them can affect external plugins with nonstandard paths.

options.title: Approve the SQLite-backed deprecation
options.body: Merge with `AuthStorage.forAgent(agentDir)` as the canonical API and preserve the documented warning/removal window for the two deprecated path-based adapters.

options.title: Preserve path semantics temporarily
options.body: Keep deprecated adapters mapped to their legacy path behavior until a published-plugin reader sweep or a later major migration, accepting continued file-backed compatibility complexity.

options.title: Pause for ecosystem evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers have evidence about published plugins using nonstandard path-based auth storage.

recommendation.title: Approve the SQLite-backed deprecation
recommendation.body: Merge with `AuthStorage.forAgent(agentDir)` as the canonical API and preserve the documented warning/removal window for the two deprecated path-based adapters.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor owns the proposed compatibility design and accompanying migration proof, though final API direction requires a repository maintainer decision.
